title: Assistant surface patterns lab journal
body:
Context / goal:
This is a personal lab journal for prototyping a small, consistent set of "assistant surface" patterns that product teams can drop into their apps. Focus: lightweight, composable UI primitives that optimize for latency, cost, and perceptual continuity when backed by Redwood inference.

Why this?
- We keep getting ad-hoc surfaces from different product teams (cards, micro-prompts, inline clarifiers) with inconsistent behavior and cost surprises.
- Goal: provide 3–5 vetted patterns + integration guidance (SDK hooks, caching middleware, telemetry) so teams can ship fast and avoid regressing on cost/latency.

Scope (working hypotheses):
- Pattern set should cover: one-shot card, progressive summary (streaming -> condensed), clarifying-question microflow, on-demand tool-launcher, and a compact reply composer (autosuggest).
- Each pattern will have: expected token budget, p95 latency target, fallback behaviour when model times out / errors, and UX affordances for perceived speed.

Quick pattern sketches (notes):
1) One-shot card
   - Trigger: explicit user request (button) or API call from a click-to-ask flow
   - UX: skeleton -> streaming text -> final card (meta: model name + confidence tag)
   - Tech: prefer smaller quantized model for brief answers; switch to larger only for long responses (auto-fork based on token estimation)
   - Telemetry: TTFB, p95 generation time, tokens consumed, fallback used

2) Progressive summary
   - Use case: longer user content (doc, thread) where user wants quick gist then optional deeper summarization
   - Flow: immediate 1-sentence summary (cheap model/embedding+template) then streaming expanded summary if user taps expand
   - Optimization: prefix-caching of the document embedding + reuse across sessions

3) Clarifying-question microflow
   - For ambiguous inputs: instead of silent assumptions, surface 1–2 clarifying options as buttons (reduces token waste)
   - Requires light intent classifier (rules or tiny model) to detect ambiguity

4) Tool launcher (compact)
   - Surface shows a few tools related to the current context (search, calendar, code-run)
   - Tools backed by secure sandbox calls — ensure gating and timeouts; show fallback when tool call fails

5) Compact reply composer (autosuggest)
   - Inline completions while user types; small token budgets per suggestion; signal to server on selection for full generation to avoid double tokens

User stories (raw):
- As a product engineer, I want a drop-in card component that streams assistant answers so my team can ship help modal faster without worrying about custom streaming logic.
- As a PM, I want cost estimates and fallbacks documented so we can set OKRs around inference spend.
- As an SRE, I want clear telemetry hooks for model fallback and queueing so alerts can be created on degraded performance.

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- Each pattern has a short integration guide + code snippets for SDKs (JS + Python).
- A small canary app demonstrates all patterns behind a single feature flag.
- Telemetry events emitted for: request-start, suggestion-render, full-response, fallback, token-count.
- Cost budget guidance: per 10k interactions baseline for each pattern (estimate ranges).

Experiment matrix (proposed):
- Variables: model family (small/medium/large), streaming vs. batch, cache enabled/disabled, prefetch embeddings yes/no
- Metrics: p95 latency, token consumption per interaction, user click-through (for suggestions), task success (manual label), error rate
- Quick A/B: progressive summary (1-sentence vs. no sentence) -> measure clicks to expand and perceived helpfulness (survey).

Implementation concerns / engineering notes:
- Session affinity: for streaming and KV cache reuse, we need sticky routing for the session's prefix state. Check with serving-runtime on affordable sticky window size. (Ping: @Rowan Blake)
- Security: tool launcher must double-check auth before invoking customer APIs. Add redaction step in client -> server to avoid leaking PII in telemetry.
- Cost accounting: map each pattern to a token-cost range and add flags to mark as high-cost in billing dashboards.

Rollout plan (rough):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): prototype UI + fake backend to validate UX flows with internal testers.
- Phase 1 (4 weeks): wire to Redwood sandbox models, implement basic telemetry and feature flag gating.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): canary behind usage cap for 5 internal teams. Collect token metrics and UX feedback.
- Phase 3: public SDK snippets + template PR for teams to adopt.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Measurement: what is the right task success label for small help flows? Quick survey, NPS per interaction, or team-defined match rate?
- Bandwidth: should we provide prebuilt Svelte + React components or minimal HTML + JS? Lean towards both but prioritize React and unstyled web components.
- Caching semantics: TTL for prefix caches when document updates live (collab editing).
- Cost guidance: need input from finance on acceptable per-user monthly inference spend for low-tier vs enterprise tier.

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Create GH branch prototype: assistant-surface/proto/with-react-widgets (ticket GH link in linked_artifacts).
- Sync with infra to ensure kv-cache metrics are exposed (ask infra: instrument KV hit/miss per session).
- Schedule 30-min demo with Mina and Rowan after phase 1 to gather integration pain points.

Rough estimates for baseline numbers (placeholders):
- One-shot card: 50–200 tokens, p95 < 400ms (small model), cost per 1k interactions: $0.40–$1.60
- Progressive summary: initial sentence 10–20 tokens (p95 < 150ms), expanded 200–800 tokens (p95 < 700ms)

If this is useful, next steps: flesh out the integration guide for the one-shot card and draft the canary app README.

-- end of lab journal entry (Rajat)
